chunks: Then it is said: How can the validity of the Imamate of Ibn al-Hasan (peace be upon him), based on the rational principles we established, coexist with the claim that the Occultation cannot have a valid reason? Is this not a contradiction? Does it not run parallel to affirming Monotheism and Divine Justice while asserting that the ambiguous verses cannot have an interpretation that conforms to these principles?
ai.seo_question: How is the Occultation of the Imam consistent with rational principles and Divine Justice?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs a rationalist analogy to refute the objection that the Imamate of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) is incompatible with the Occultation, arguing that just as ambiguous Quranic verses (Mutashabihat) possess coherent interpretations aligned with rational principles, the Occultation has a valid, albeit hidden, wisdom. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly commitment to reconciling divine decree with human reason, asserting that the absence of an immediately apparent cause does not negate the validity of the Imam's authority.
